title: Siena, Concistoro 2308 fasc. 2 no. 8: the Milan-Ferrara league slip, c. 1440-41, with its contemporary decipherment

documents.shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Siena, Concistoro 2308 fasc. 2, no. 8; DECODE R4797 (Concistoro_2308_51)
documents.date: c. 1440-41 (proposed: Felix V elected Nov 1439; Bianca Maria Visconti married Oct 1441)

plaintext.source: The clear memorandum on the upper part of the same sheet, paragraphs 5-7 ('Nel polizolo dicto segue ...').

transcription.notes: Transcribed 18 Oct 2026 (Claude) from line crops of IMG_R4797_I27940_P.jpg; cipher signs only. George Lasry counts c. 400 symbols, presumably the whole slip with its clear words.

system.summary: Simple substitution in letter-like signs, two signs for a and one for s/ss, with two name signs (duca di Milano, Viniziani).
system.sibling_key: Not compared sign by sign with the c. 1440 keys R4748 and R4749; different from nos. 7, 19 and 21.
system.notes: Key rebuilt from the contemporary decipherment (decode.py); a has two signs (2, 5).

prior_solution.where: The clear memorandum on the same sheet (ASSi Concistoro 2308 fasc. 2 no. 8, DECODE R4797).

conditions.human_role: Set the goal (decipher the letters of Concistoro 2308; try the filed keys first); passed on George Lasry's report of 17 Oct 2026 asking for one entry per key. Asked to record the disagreement between the project's 'read at the time' and George Lasry's 'unsolved'.

solution.what: Found the whole busta Concistoro 2308 on DECODE (keys R4746-R4789, letters R4790-R4814, R1858) and downloaded the images with the project cookie (survey entry siena1421).
Indexed the 43 key records of fasc. 1 (1433 Petrucci, c. 1440 frate Bernardino and R4749, 1454 Milan ambassadors, Casole, 1478 Bichi, c. 1500 and 16th-c. keys).
Inventory: no. 8 taken as read at the time, a ciphered slip below a clear memorandum naming papa Felice, the Duke of Milan, Leonello d'Este, Niccolo Piccinino; no sign aligned.
George Lasry's report lists no. 8 as unsolved, c. 400 symbols, no interlinear plaintext; a relation to the clear memorandum above 'possible but speculative'.
The slip transcribed sign by sign from line crops at 3-4x: 166 cipher signs, 23 types, in four runs between the clear words.

The memorandum's catchwords 'Anchora disse' and 'antiveduto questo' found as clear words of the slip; the runs aligned letter for letter with paragraphs 5-7 ('Nel polizolo dicto segue ...'): 5 9 T 9 5 = aveva, F T W W 2 W 2 = ferrara, L T Z PHI T L L Z = leonello.
Key rebuilt from the alignment: 21 letter signs (two for a, S for s/ss, 9 for u/v/b) and two name signs (duca di Milano, Viniziani); decode.py.
decode.py applies the key to all four runs: every sign reads, spelling variants only against the memorandum.
Key consistency: each sign keeps one value across all four runs (7 = d in dato, madonna, di, de, udirete; 2 and 5 = a throughout).
Split out of the survey entry siena1421 under the one-key rule; the project's 'read at the time' and George Lasry's 'unsolved' recorded side by side.

A second, independent alignment by a parallel session (main commit 883fa6f41, made without transcripts/no08.txt or decode.py, in its own sign names): image re-fetched with the DECODE cookie and three cipher passages aligned with the memorandum at 2x: '÷ 59t95 75□ø I2 7øϕϕ2 9ff2ϕ +c5' = '[duca di Milano] aveva dato [ma]donna biancha' (aveva = ABCBA), 'I2ɷ+ctɱt' = 'marchese' twice, 'o-tɷɷ2ɷ2' = 'ferrara', 't ϕøϕ ff9ø I2ϕ+c2 ot +ct' = 'e non può manchare che'. Its values are those of decode.py under other names; its one doubt (sign I in 'la' and 'manchare') is settled by the 166-sign reading: the cipher has 'madonna', I = m throughout.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): transcripts/no08.txt / no08.tok; decode.py output saved to texts/no08_decryption.txt (each run beside the memorandum's words); key key.json

Verify v8: no08_reading.md rescored after capitalising the resolved name signs and dropping the run-edge marks: 1.0 explicit holes (4/4), hole rate 0; every word carried by the contemporary memorandum. Keeps read, as a reading of four fragments.

outcome.method_basis: The contemporary decipherment is on the same sheet (memorandum paragraphs 5-7, 'Nel polizolo dicto segue'); the slip was transcribed and aligned with it sign by sign, and the key rebuilt from the alignment reads every cipher sign.
outcome.fraction_read_source: decode.py over transcripts/no08.tok: 166 of 166 cipher signs given a value; 6 doubtful signs listed in NOTES

gaps.detail: in a covering letter not on this sheet and not among the DECODE photographs; its decipherment is on the memorandum

credits.note: The clear memorandum on the same sheet, c. 1440-41, deciphering the slip (paragraphs 5-7).

outcome.notes: George Lasry's report (17 Oct 2026) lists no. 8 as unsolved and calls the relation to the memorandum speculative; the alignment of 18 Oct 2026 shows the memorandum is its decipherment. To be confirmed with him.

texts.label: Siena, Concistoro 2308 fasc. 2 no. 8 (DECODE R4797), c. 1440-41
texts.summary: A ciphered slip on the Milan-Ferrara league: the league between the Duke of Milan and the Marquis of Ferrara against the Venetians and their league, the Duke of Milan having given 'madonna Biancha' to messer Leonello, the Marquis's son, and 'grandissimi facti' to be expected. The clear memorandum on the same sheet (paragraphs 5-7) is its contemporary decipherment; the key rebuilt from the alignment reads all 166 signs.

reading_review.note: Verify v8, 23 Oct 2026: a reading of fragments. The slip mixes clear words and four cipher runs; texts/no08_reading.md gives the runs only (the clear text between them is not transcribed). Scored 0.50 because the two resolved name signs were written lower-case ([duca di Milano]) and the run-edge '…' marks (clear text, not unread cipher) counted as holes; with the name signs capitalised and the marks dropped: 1.0 on explicit holes (4/4), 0.25 plain (1440 Sienese spelling), hole rate 0. Each run is a clause that holds (the league between the Duke of Milan and the Marquis of Ferrara; the Venetians and their league; Bianca given to Leonello; 'grandisimi fatti'), and every word is confirmed letter for letter by the contemporary memorandum on the same sheet (paragraphs 5-7). Not 'not prose' (it is running sentences), not decoded-only (no hole).
